officialSummary: In terms of GOI notification F.No. 4(5)-B(W&M)/2021 dated October 21, 2021 (SGB 2021-22 Series VII - Issue date November 02, 2021) on Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme, premature redemption of Gold Bond may be permitted after fifth year from the date of issue of such Gold Bond on the date on which interest is payable. Accordingly, the due date of premature redemption of the above tranche shall be on November 02, 2026. 2. Further, the redemption price of SGB shall be based on simple average of closing price of gold of 999 purity of previous three business days from the date of redemption, as published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd (IBJA). Accordingly, the redemption price for premature redemption due on November 02, 2026, shall be ₹14,167/- (Rupees Fourteen Thousand One Hundred and Sixty-Seven Only) per unit of SGB based on the simple average of closing price of gold for the three business days i.e., October 28, October 29, and October 30, 2026. Ajit Prasad Deputy General Manager (Communications) Press Release: 2026-2027/1419

officialSummary: Data on lending and deposit rates of scheduled commercial banks (SCBs) (excluding regional rural banks and small finance banks) received during October 2026 are set out in Tables 1 to 9. Highlights: Lending Rates: The weighted average lending rate (WALR) on outstanding rupee loans of SCBs remained unchanged at 8.96 per cent in September 2026 compared to August 2026. The WALR on fresh rupee loans of SCBs declined to 8.51 per cent in September 2026 from 8.61 per cent in August 2026. 1-Year median Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR) of SCBs declined to 8.55 per cent in October 2026 from 8.61 per cent in September 2026. The WALR on fresh as well as outstanding rupee loans exhibited a mixed movement across sectors in September 2026. Deposit Rates: The weighted average domestic term deposit rate (WADTDR) on outstanding rupee term deposits of SCBs marginally declined to 6.55 per cent in September 2026 from 6.56 per cent in August 2026. The WADTDR on fresh rupee term deposits of SCBs declined to 5.61 per cent in September 2026 from 5.67 per cent in August 2026. officialSummary: Data on sectoral deployment of bank credit for the month of September 2026, collected from 41 select scheduled commercial banks (SCBs), which together account for about 95 per cent of the total non-food credit by all SCBs 1 , are set out in Statements I and II . On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, non-food bank credit 2 grew by 19.1 per cent as on the fortnight ended September 30, 2026, compared to 11.2 per cent during the corresponding fortnight of the previous year (i.e., October 03, 2025). Highlights of the sectoral deployment of bank credit as on the fortnight ended September 30, 2026, are given below: Credit to agriculture and allied activities registered a y-o-y growth of 19.5 per cent vis-a-vis 8.9 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of the previous year. Credit to industry recorded a y-o-y growth of 19.5 per cent (7.7 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of last year). While credit to ‘large’ and ‘medium’ industries grew at an accelerated pace, ‘micro and small’ industries exhibited steady growth. Among major industries, credit to ‘infrastructure’, ‘basic metal and metal products’, ‘all engineering’, ‘chemical and chemical products’, ‘food processing’ and ‘textiles’ marked buoyant y-o-y growth. Credit to services sector registered a y-o-y growth of 28.3 per cent (9.9 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of the previous year), supported by buoyant growth in segments such as ‘non-banking financial companies’ (NBFCs), ‘trade’ ‘commercial real estate’, ‘transport operators’ and ‘professional services’. Credit to personal loans segment recorded a y-o-y growth of 17.3 per cent, as compared with 11.5 per cent a year ago. While credit growth in segments such as ‘housing’ and ‘vehicle loans’ remained resilient, ‘advances against fixed deposits’ accelerated. Growth in ‘loans against gold jewellery’ and ‘education’ decelerated compared to last year, albeit it remained strong. Ajit Prasad Deputy General Manager (Communications) Press Release: 2026-2027/1412 1 Dat
title: Sectoral Deployment of Bank Credit – September 2026
